title: A2UI Express separates UI generation from rendering
dek: Google introduces a compact inference format that compiles into validated A2UI messages, reducing model output while keeping rendering under client control.
evidence: Google vendor measurements; independent replication pending
takeaway: Prototype A2UI Express against direct JSON on representative financial workflows. Measure end-to-end latency, valid render rate, authorization checks and correction cost before selecting a generation format.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Traditional generative UI asks a model to emit verbose A2UI JSON messages. Tokens and validation cost make complex screens slow to appear.

paragraphs: The bottleneck: Traditional generative UI asks a model to emit verbose A2UI JSON messages. Tokens and validation cost make complex screens slow to appear.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: A2UI Express uses compact assignment-like syntax; an SDK compiler turns it into validated A2UI JSON for the same trusted component catalog and renderer.
The model chooses from an approved catalog. The client retains component rendering and server actions keep their own authorization checks.

paragraphs: Shorter intermediate format: A2UI Express uses compact assignment-like syntax; an SDK compiler turns it into validated A2UI JSON for the same trusted component catalog and renderer.
No generated executable UI code: The model chooses from an approved catalog. The client retains component rendering and server actions keep their own authorization checks.

example.caption: Same card, different model output
example.takeaway: Express replaces repeated field names with short assignments. The SDK compiles them into A2UI JSON for the same renderer.
example.note: Schematic example; the JSON excerpt omits surface creation. Not benchmark data.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: Google reports up to 3× fewer output tokens and up to 3× lower latency than Direct JSON in its 51-task Gemini 3.5 Flash format study.
Direct JSON can stream components; Express waits for full output before compilation. End-to-end completion and time to first useful render can move differently.
A constrained decision model such as Jev may choose predefined layouts faster (Google cites up to 80× faster layout decisions), but it cannot generate arbitrary catalog trees.

paragraphs: Vendor measurements: Google reports up to 3× fewer output tokens and up to 3× lower latency than Direct JSON in its 51-task Gemini 3.5 Flash format study.
First-render caveat: Direct JSON can stream components; Express waits for full output before compilation. End-to-end completion and time to first useful render can move differently.
Another approach: A constrained decision model such as Jev may choose predefined layouts faster (Google cites up to 80× faster layout decisions), but it cannot generate arbitrary catalog trees.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Use predetermined layouts when the workflow is known; choose Express when the model needs compositional freedom.
Compare first useful render, total completion, schema correctness, denied actions and cost for equal tasks—not token count alone.

paragraphs: Pick by screen shape: Use predetermined layouts when the workflow is known; choose Express when the model needs compositional freedom.
